P01.note: Key rests on combining the broken joint rate with papers retreating to purely city coverage; 'hamstrung' (papers shrank to eight pages) remains a close second, and 'dethroned' is half-supported by advertisers leaving.

P02.note: Sand dropped in hollows plus straight furrows and even wheat yields 'leveled'; 'nourished' is killed by wheat no thicker in the hollows, 'irrigated' literally describes the flooding.

P03.note: Must combine 1490s beams vs 1580 completion with the builder's youth on the hill to reverse the apparent direction; 'replica' and 'offshoot' fit the matching order and dragons if the dates are missed. 'Its oldest beams' has an ambiguous 'its'.

P04.note: The exclusive-contract sentence decides it alone; 'designed from scratch' kills mimicked and 'judged equal' kills leapfrogged.

P05.note: Cod shelter under the ice and are eaten where no ice forms, so 'roof'; 'almost nothing grows' kills pantry, perch/raft lean on the seals and birds the passage never puts on the ice.

P06.note: Miners camped in the churchyard until the council stopped meeting; the final sentence (same families, same fields, street still facing the landing) explicitly kills ruined, reoriented and repopulated.

P07.note: Leaders at home direct everything ('headquarters' killed), the café only presents the case to diplomats and parliament, so 'embassy'; 'hub' is a near-miss that fits most of the passage.

P08.note: One family owns every palm and well and ships the dates out, so 'estate'; 'could buy nothing there' kills emporium and fairground.

P09.note: The relocation sentence (capital to market town, camel to mule) decides 'domesticated'; 'all eleven episodes remained... as long' kills distilled and honed.

P10.note: City bread came from merchants at fluctuating prices, killing ballast/backstop; the granary was used to buy out a defiant lord's market, so 'cudgel'.

P11.note: 'Each June the town's pageant is played on that platform before most of the town' hands over arena; bazaar fails on a surface read (no trade anywhere) and cesspool is off-register for level turf drained to the river. Only bunker (galleries) is a real distractor.

P12.note: Hatchery is off the passage's topic (no breeding mentioned). Uncrossable chute plus animals on the log every night and the worn moss strip give highway; hostel/garden are thin.

P13.note: Single opening and an upright candle flame kill chimney and bellows; the basin the village draws from gives cistern, while 'same mild temperature all year' makes cooler a literal near-fit.

P14.note: Strains sown in strips beside local wheat and results published gives testbed; seed ordered from the breeder kills wellspring and stopgap (the closed merchant is a lure). Yardstick is a strong near-miss since the station compared strains.

P15.note: Equal duck predation kills manipulated and equal bacterial death kills immunized; smaller size, fewer eggs and an unchanged lifespan favor 'milked', but neutered is defensible from the reduced eggs, though they still lay a third.

P16.note: One day's stop in burrows then moving on, never trapped twice, gives inn; lair is killed by 'never twice', lane by the east-west hedge crossing a north-bound route, larder baited by voles.

P17.note: Scattered open pits with forest between gives pitted; 'dug out from above' kills riddled (tunnels), the cairn and forest kill razed, trout kill poisoned.

P18.note: Uniform layers 'whatever the weather' and others dating cores against its count point to a timekeeper, metronome; ledger (exact count of years) is close. Shared shrimp and plankton lure microcosm.

P19.note: Schoolhouse is off topic. The sheds holding shipped-whole cars until dealers called decide warehouse; 'sold cars... since 1930' kills toehold.

P20.note: Dry riffles plus bends sinking to cracked mud gives parched; the bends sentence kills pooled, the near-miss after the riffles dry.

P21.note: Digging through layers to doorways gives smothered; benchmarks at 1880 height kill tilted and submerged (the leaning lighthouse is the literal lure), burial kills scoured.

P22.note: Drifting bodies tugged back so the edge stays sharp gives shepherd; equal impacts in both runs kills umbrella, tether and slingshot remain plausible near-misses.

P23.note: Barred from new members, union dies out by attrition: doomed. Let stand kills disbanded, won strikes kill defanged, struck together kills divided.

P24.note: Overpaint removed revealing figures beneath gives uncovered; scrubbed literally fits the solvent and the smoke; panels going back as they came out kills transferred.

P25.note: Stores water behind the ice dam then releases it gives valve; the warm July outflow kills thermostat, the release kills sink.

P26.note: Population steady but workers and shopping went south and stores closed: drained. The road on the riverbank below town kills fragmented; fossilized and engulfed fit parts of the passage.

P27.note: Boats ride out winter behind it while other ports haul out: breakwater. A deep gap for any ship kills barricade and chokepoint, ending short of the island kills causeway.

P28.note: Every fish sold the same morning to the same number of buyers, a third going for fertilizer: saturated. The price collapse kills steadied; stifled is the near-miss.

P29.note: 'Every book stood in its place... the catalog matched the shelves card for card' kills plundered, pulped and purged on a surface read; all three destructive P-words fail together, leaving the only non-destructive option.

P30.note: Automatic raise/cut rule damping prices gives regulator; 'five of them cuts' kills ratchet, pendulum and pacemaker fit loosely.

P31.note: Mortuary fails on a surface read (no burials). The wall facing the ford, spear tips and crossing-week hearths give lookout; the riverside camp with bedding and children kills lodge; the freezing back chamber is the icebox lure.

P32.note: Songs carried to the mill cities by records and played there: transplanted. 'Whole and in the old rough style' kills smoothed and stripped; singers leaving kills silenced.

P33.note: Clear water sinking through salt-crusted sand, then yields matching the upper slopes, means the salt was washed out: rinsed. Clear snowmelt kills replenished, bare fallow kills reseeded, standing stubble kills plowed.

P34.note: Tip cut back 400 yards with width unchanged: blunted. Driving the crest road to the light kills cleaved, 'as wide as before' kills broadened, further erosion kills armored.

P35.note: City wall on its bank, beyond the watch's reach, duke's tax across: border. Too shallow for barges kills artery, brackish kills aqueduct.

P36.note: Coal warehouses that steamships call at every voyage: depot. Shelled without reply kills fortress, sailing ships passing by undercuts haven.

P37.note: Families and cattle ferried over in floods: ark. Raiders burning its barns kills citadel, too deep to wade kills crossing, too fast to tie up kills anchorage.

P38.note: Bank lump sum, half-yearly repayments, deed back after the last payment: mortgaged. The deed returning kills liquidated, the oak woods lure logged.

P39.note: Hacked church plate plus coins minted within a few years, pushed hastily into a scrape, give loot; insurance (buried savings) is the strong near-miss and the scrape only weakly rules it out.

P40.note: 'A fine brown web showed in the glaze... did not wash out' names crazing outright, so cracked comes from one sentence; 'smooth to the fingertip' kills blistered, 'clear as ever' kills clouded; brown makes blackened a literal lure.
